title: Trilobatin attenuates cerebral ischaemia/reperfusion-induced blood-brain barrier dysfunction by targeting matrix metalloproteinase 9: The legend of a food additive.
authors: Feng, Linying; Li, Yeli; Lin, Mu; Xie, Dianyou; Luo, Yunmei; Zhang, Yuandong; He, Zhixu; Gong, Qihai; Zhun, Zhu Yi; Gao, Jianmei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究食品添加剂Trilobatin通过靶向MMP9保护脑缺血再灌注血脑屏障，虽含分子对接但核心是疾病病理与药物机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) breakdown is one of the crucial pathological changes of cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. Trilobatin (TLB), a naturally occurring food additive, exerts neuroprotective effects against cerebral I/R injury as demonstrated in our previous study. This study was designed to investigate the effect of TLB on BBB disruption after cerebral I/R injury. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Rats with focal cerebral ischaemia caused by transient middle cerebral artery occlusion were studied along with brain microvascular endothelial cells and human astrocytes to mimic BBB injury caused by oxygen and glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). KEY RESULTS: The results showed that TLB effectively maintained BBB integrity and inhibited neuronal loss following cerebral I/R challenge. Furthermore, TLB increased tight junction proteins including ZO-1, Occludin and Claudin 5, and decreased the levels of apolipoprotein E (APOE) 4, cyclophilin A (CypA) and phosphorylated nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kappaB), thereby reducing proinflammatory cytokines. TLB also decreased the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio and cleaved-caspase 3 levels along with a reduced number of apoptotic neurons. Molecular docking and transcriptomics predicted MMP9 as a prominent gene evoked by TLB treatment. The protective effects of TLB on cerebral I/R-induced BBB breakdown was largely abolished by overexpression of MMP9, and the beneficial effects of TLB on OGD/R-induced loss of BBB integrity in human brain microvascular endothelial cells and astrocyte co-cultures was markedly reinforced by knockdown of MMP9. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Our findings reveal a novel property of TLB: preventing BBB disruption following cerebral I/R via targeting MMP9 and inhibiting APOE4/CypA/NF-kappaB axis.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：血脑屏障（BBB）破坏是脑缺血再灌注（I/R）损伤的关键病理变化之一。三叶苷（TLB）作为一种天然食品添加剂，在我们先前的研究中已证明其对脑I/R损伤具有神经保护作用。本研究旨在探讨TLB对脑I/R损伤后BBB破坏的影响。实验方法：采用短暂大脑中动脉阻塞引起局灶性脑缺血的大鼠模型，并结合脑微血管内皮细胞和人星形胶质细胞，模拟氧糖剥夺/复氧（OGD/R）引起的BBB损伤。关键结果：结果表明，TLB有效维持BBB完整性，并抑制脑I/R损伤后的神经元丢失。此外，TLB增加紧密连接蛋白（包括ZO-1、Occludin和Claudin 5），降低载脂蛋白E（APOE）4、亲环蛋白A（CypA）和磷酸化核因子κB（NF-kappaB）的水平，从而减少促炎细胞因子。TLB还降低Bax/Bcl-2比值和cleaved-caspase 3水平，并减少凋亡神经元数量。分子对接和转录组学预测MMP9为TLB处理诱导的显著基因。MMP9过表达可基本消除TLB对脑I/R诱导的BBB破坏的保护作用，而MMP9敲低则显著增强TLB对OGD/R诱导的人脑微血管内皮细胞和星形胶质细胞共培养中BBB完整性丧失的有益效果。结论与意义：我们的发现揭示了TLB的新特性：通过靶向MMP9并抑制APOE4/CypA/NF-kappaB轴，预防脑I/R后的BBB破坏。
